references.text: The parable of the unmerciful servant, where the king forgives the debt of a servant who cannot pay – parallel to the lender forgiving the debts of the two debtors.
In the Lord's Prayer we ask that God will forgive us our debts, just as we forgive our debtors – the same theme of debt forgiveness as an image of forgiveness.
Jesus explains the point of the parable: the one who is forgiven much loves much – a direct answer to the question of who will love most.
The preceding verses that set up the parable with the two debtors, which form the context for the question about forgiveness and love.
Paul writes that God has forgiven us all our debts – the same image of debt forgiveness as an expression of God's grace.
An exhortation to forgive one another, just as God has forgiven us in Christ – the theme of forgiveness as a response to God's grace.
Christ died for us while we were still helpless and sinners – parallel to the fact that the debtors had nothing to pay with, yet were forgiven.
Jesus says that we should do good and lend without expecting anything back – the theme of grace and generosity in connection with debt.
We love because he loved us first – parallel to the idea that the one who receives forgiveness responds with love, as illustrated by the parable.
